decisions.reason: As a newly launched particle-therapy phantom tied to the firm's core dosimetry business and publicly introduced on its own page, management would likely continue despite the delayed US rollout because recent launch issues can still be framed as temporary.

This chamber fits the firm's established measurement portfolio, and because it has already been publicly launched and likely required specialized development and certification effort, management would be inclined to persist with it.
Although another small-volume chamber may create some overlap risk, the firm's public commitment and sunk development costs make withdrawal so soon after launch unlikely.
A full standard clinical ionization chamber product line with several models signals substantial investment and visible commitment, which strongly favors keeping it on the market.

Because this relative dosimetry chamber is close to the firm's core offering and has already been marketed directly, management would likely justify staying the course rather than admit an early reversal.
This thimble chamber is a conventional, strategically coherent extension of the firm's radiation-measurement range, so escalation of commitment makes an early discontinuation unlikely.
